resources.string: Through SSH your Mac keeps its own size. In the device\'s size it comes directly: in the same Wi-Fi, or with the Tailscale app\'s VPN on.
Through aOS\'s Tailscale your Mac keeps its own size. In the device\'s size it comes with the Tailscale app\'s VPN on, or in the same Wi-Fi.
Kept on this device behind its screen lock. It only goes to the Mac\'s screen sharing, through the SSH connection or directly in the same network.
Set a screen lock for this device first (Settings > Security).
Screens in the device\'s size

Both screens take the device\'s shape and turn with it: aOS resizes the workspace\'s display, your Mac gets a virtual display in Open Screen Sharing\'s high performance mode, directly in the same Wi-Fi or with the Tailscale app\'s VPN. Through SSH alone your Mac keeps its own size. More resolution gives more room and less sharpness.

The screen of the workspace and of the Mac is based on Open Screen Sharing by nekohasekai, used under the GNU General Public License, version 3. aOS changed it for its own use: the screens are reached through the connection to your Mac (your Mac in the device\'s size also directly), and aOS\'s sign-in replaces the app\'s own.
They keep running when the connection drops, also with the app closed, and this device picks up where it left off. End the ones you no longer need.
Open on this device
aOS on the Mac now takes requests only when this device signs them, with a key it gets when you pair. Show the pairing code on the Mac and scan it.
This device loses the connection until the Mac wakes up again (open the lid or press a key). The workspace and your agents pause meanwhile.
The device talks to your Mac over SSH with a key that never leaves this device.
aOS on your device
Set a screen lock for this device first (the device\'s settings > Security). Approving a sign-in needs your fingerprint, face or screen lock.
This code is from a newer aOS. Update the app on this device.
This device makes its own key. Only its public half goes to the Mac.
Pair only with your own Mac. aOS on the Mac adds this device\'s key to your user\'s SSH keys there.
How the device reaches it
On the go through aOS\'s own Tailscale. After pairing, set it up on this device too, with the same Tailscale account.
On the go through the Tailscale app. On this device you need it too, signed in with the same account (or aOS\'s own Tailscale, in Settings > Connection).
Only on the same network: on the go the device doesn\'t reach this Mac.
The device accepts the Mac only with exactly this key, now and later.
Name of this device
The device now reaches your Mac by itself whenever the app is open.
The Mac didn\'t answer. Check that the device is on the same network as the Mac and that the pairing code is still shown.
The Mac\'s answer wasn\'t understood. Update aOS on the Mac and on this device.
Pair again to keep approving from this device.
Update aOS on the Mac to see the workspace from this device.
The Mac no longer accepts this device. Pair again in aOS on the Mac.
The Mac isn\'t reachable. On the go, set up aOS\'s Tailscale on this device: Settings > Connection.
The Mac isn\'t reachable, and aOS\'s Tailscale on this device isn\'t connected (Settings > Connection).
The Mac isn\'t reachable. On the go, switch on Tailscale on this device (the Tailscale app, or aOS\'s Tailscale in Settings > Connection).
This device
SSH key of this device
This device forgets the Mac. To remove the device\'s key from the Mac too, open aOS on the Mac and remove it from the paired devices.
Sign-in requests and help requests from this Mac no longer reach this device.
To log in to another computer with this device\'s key, add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys there. The public key isn\'t secret.
The private key was made in this device\'s secure hardware and can\'t leave it.
The private key is in this device\'s keystore without secure hardware and is never synced.
They stay in your Bitwarden account. aOS on your Mac signs in to it with Bitwarden\'s own command line tool; this device never talks to Bitwarden.
aOS on your Mac then gets exactly that login from Bitwarden and types it into the workspace. Neither the device nor the Mac keeps it.
The device reaches your Mac over SSH (the Mac\'s Remote Login), with a key made on this device that never leaves it. The Mac\'s key is checked every time.
The Mac account name and password for its screen stay on this device, encrypted, and only go to the Mac\'s screen sharing.
aOS\'s own Tailscale on this device is Tailscale\'s open source code (tailscale.com), under the BSD 3-Clause License.
The device tries the same network first, then the tailnet, then the Mac\'s name on the network.
Tailscale app on this device
Your Mac uses the Tailscale app. On this device the Tailscale app, signed in with the same account, reaches it too; so does aOS\'s own Tailscale below.
aOS\'s Tailscale on this device
No VPN and no Tailscale app needed. aOS only reaches your Mac through it, and nothing on this device is reachable in your tailnet. Its keys stay on this device, out of backups.
aOS can bring Tailscale along on this device too: no VPN, no extra app. You sign in once with your Tailscale account, the same as on the Mac.
Signed in. The tailnet\'s admin still has to approve this device in the Tailscale admin console.
Sign Out removes this device from the tailnet and deletes its Tailscale keys here.
Sign out of Tailscale on this device?
This device leaves your tailnet. On the go it then reaches the Mac only through the Tailscale app, if it has it.
